prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1235; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim number.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the accident happened?
A: I was driving on a main road in Houston, Texas, heading toward the grocery store near my house. It was early afternoon and traffic was moderate.

Q: Can you describe what happened?
A: I was in the left lane preparing to turn. A vehicle coming the other way drifted over the center line and hit my front end. It wasn't a hard hit. We both almost stopped right away.

Q: How fast were you traveling?
A: I'd say maybe fifteen or twenty miles an hour. I had just slowed down for the turn.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, I always do.

Q: Did the airbags deploy?
A: No, they didn't. The car just jolted forward and back.

Q: Did you feel any injuries at the scene?
A: Not right away. My neck felt stiff, and by the next morning my right shoulder was really sore. It hurts when I reach overhead or lift anything heavy.

Q: Have you seen a doctor about the shoulder?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care two days later. They took X-rays and told me to rest it and start physical therapy.

Q: Have you had any prior injuries to that shoulder?
A: No, nothing serious. I played some recreational softball years ago, but I never had any treatment for it.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: No, I think that covers it. I just hope I can get back to normal soon.
